simple.meaning: עֲשַׂר (ʻăsar) is a Hebrew object word meaning “ten.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Ezra 6:17. The surrounding context includes offering, kingship, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עֲשַׂר (H6236) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: עֲשַׂר (ʻăsar) / H6236 is traced through Ezra 6:17, Daniel 4:26, Daniel 7:7, Daniel 7:20 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.full: H6236. asar or asrah עַשְׂרָה עֲשַׂר, noun masculine and feminine a ten (see Biblical Hebrew); — masculine (following feminine noun ) Dan 7:7 , 20 , 24 ; feminine (before masculine noun ) Dan 7:24 ; עֲשַׂר תְּרֵי = twelve (following masculine noun ) 4:26 ; Ezra 6:17 .

occurrences.englishText: They offered at the dedication of this house of God one hundred bulls, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs; and for a sin offering for all Israel, twelve male goats, according to the number of the tribes of Israel.
Whereas they commanded to leave the stump of the roots of the tree; your kingdom shall be sure to you, after that you will have known that the heavens do rule.

“After this I saw in the night visions, and, behold, there was a fourth animal, awesome and powerful, and exceedingly strong. It had great iron teeth. It devoured and broke in pieces, and stamped the residue with its feet. It was different from all the animals that were before it. It had ten horns.

and concerning the ten horns that were on its head, and the other horn which came up, and before which three fell, even that horn that had eyes, and a mouth that spoke great things, whose look was more stout than its fellows.
As for the ten horns, ten kings will arise out of this kingdom. Another will arise after them; and he will be different from the former, and he will put down three kings.
